question: Why do patients with metabolic acidosis often have abnormal potassium levels too?

options.A: Acidosis causes the pancreas to stop releasing insulin into the blood
options.B: The liver stores excess potassium whenever blood pH rises above normal
options.C: Potassium is directly converted into bicarbonate inside the glomerulus
options.D: Hydrogen and potassium ions share similar transport pathways in the kidneys

explanation: Think of hydrogen and potassium as rivals sharing the same doorway in the kidney. When there's too much acid (hydrogen), it affects how potassium is handled, often leading to a potassium imbalance.

question: Which group of patients has the highest risk of getting burned or injured by hot and cold packs?

options.A: Patients with decreased sensory perception
options.B: Young adults with minor sports bruises
options.C: Patients who are fully alert and active
options.D: Athletes with normal muscle tone

explanation: Always be extra careful with patients who can't feel hot or cold properly—they won't be able to warn you if the pack is hurting their skin!

question: How often should you turn an immobile, very ill patient to protect their skin?

options.A: Only when soiled
options.B: Once every shift
options.C: Every six hours
options.D: Every two hours

explanation: The golden rule of positioning! Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas and stops bedsores before they start.

question: A patient is having a hard time buttoning their shirt and holding a toothbrush after a stroke. Who should step in to help with these daily tasks?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients regain fine motor skills for daily activities like dressing, eating, and brushing teeth.

question: What is another common name for therapeutic dietary counselling?

options.A: Holistic wellness education
options.B: Preventive lifestyle coaching
options.C: Medical nutrition therapy
options.D: General community wellness

explanation: Therapeutic counselling uses specific food and nutrient adjustments to treat active illnesses, which is known as medical nutrition therapy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: Why is looking at a trend of vital signs over several hours so much better than just checking a single set of numbers?

options.A: It is required for billing and insurance records
options.B: It proves the machine is working properly
options.C: It shows the direction the patient's health is moving
options.D: It replaces the need for physician physical exams

explanation: Exactly! Tracking numbers over time helps you spot a slow, steady slip in a patient's condition, even if their current numbers still technically look 'normal.'

question: What do we call the long, multi-celled structure formed when individual muscle-building cells (myoblasts) fuse together?

options.A: Myotube
options.B: Myofibril
options.C: Sarcomere
options.D: Sarcolemma

explanation: When myoblasts join forces, they form a tube-like structure called a myotube before maturing into full muscle fibers. You are mastering the vocabulary!

question: How does carbon monoxide poisoning cause internal suffocation?

options.A: It directly paralyzes the diaphragm muscle
options.B: It triggers immediate swelling of the vocal cords
options.C: It causes the lungs to fill with fluid rapidly
options.D: It binds to hemoglobin and blocks oxygen delivery

explanation: Carbon monoxide is sneaky—it loves sticking to your red blood cells (hemoglobin) way more than oxygen does. Even if the patient is breathing fine, their tissues still starve because the seats on the transport truck are all taken!

question: What is the medical term for natural, age-related hearing loss?

options.A: Otosclerosis
options.B: Barotrauma
options.C: Tympanitis
options.D: Presbycusis

explanation: Spot on! Presbycusis is just the natural wear-and-tear on our hearing as we grow older, usually starting with high-pitched sounds.

question: Why do routine medical checks in schools help find vision and hearing issues early?

options.A: Teachers are trained ophthalmologists and audiologists
options.B: Children rarely complain about mild sensory deficits on their own
options.C: Parents deliberately hide medical test results from school authorities
options.D: Sensory problems only develop while children are inside classrooms

explanation: Exactly! Kids often think everyone sees or hears just like they do, so they won't realize they have a problem unless we check.

question: What happens when a patient takes an anticonvulsant that induces liver enzymes along with their oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: The liver stops processing all medications completely for 24 hours
options.B: The birth control pills are broken down faster, reducing their effectiveness
options.C: The anticonvulsant stops working and breakthrough seizures occur instantly
options.D: The contraceptive hormones build up in the blood to toxic levels

explanation: Certain seizure meds rev up the liver's metabolism like a sports car. This means oral contraceptives get broken down and cleared out way too fast, putting the patient at risk of an unplanned pregnancy.

question: What term describes the study of what the body does to a drug (absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion)?

options.A: Pharmacokinetics
options.B: Pharmacogenetics
options.C: Pharmacodynamics
options.D: Pharmaceutics

explanation: Nailed it! Pharmacokinetics tracks the journey of the drug through the body across those four famous ADME stages.

question: What is the primary action of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine in shock?

options.A: Dissolve blood clots in the coronary arteries
options.B: Dilate the bronchial tubes in the lungs
options.C: Slow down a rapid heart rate
options.D: Constrict blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors cause blood vessels to tighten, which increases vascular resistance and helps raise blood pressure when fluids are not enough. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: What should a nurse do if a sound-minded patient at home refuses treatment?

options.A: Respect the refusal and document the discussion thoroughly
options.B: Call the police to arrest the family members
options.C: Force the patient to take the treatment immediately
options.D: Ignore the refusal and administer the drug secretly

explanation: Exactly right! Competent patients have every right to decide what happens to their bodies, including saying no to treatment.

question: What important clinical step must a nurse take before starting a returning defaulter on a new hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: Require the client to pay a fine for defaulting
options.B: Wait for laboratory tests that take three weeks
options.C: Carefully rule out existing pregnancy
options.D: Consult the national ministry of health directly

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out pregnancy before dispensing or administering new hormonal methods to protect both client and baby.

question: Which position is best when placing the rectal tip for a barium enema?

options.A: Sims' position (lying on the left side with right knee bent)
options.B: Supine position (flat on the back)
options.C: Prone position (lying flat on the tummy)
options.D: Lithotomy position (stirrups up)

explanation: The Sims' position naturally relaxes the anal sphincter, making the insertion smoother, safer, and much more comfortable for the patient.

question: You listen to all four areas of a patient's tummy for five full minutes and hear zero sounds. What does this mean?

options.A: Absent bowel sounds indicating decreased motility
options.B: Normal digestion happening very quietly
options.C: Mild gas trapped in the lower colon
options.D: Hyperactive sounds due to recent eating

explanation: Total silence for a full five minutes is a red flag! It usually means the intestines have slowed right down or stopped moving.

question: How does buying fruits and vegetables in their natural season help a household manage its food budget?

options.A: Purchasing seasonal items prevents the need to cook meals
options.B: In-season produce is typically more abundant and therefore cheaper
options.C: Out-of-season crops always contain more vitamins
options.D: Seasonal foods require chemical preservatives to stay fresh

explanation: High local supply during harvest seasons drives down the cost of fruits and vegetables while maintaining high nutritional quality. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h3)

question: What does the 'teach-back' method mean when teaching a patient?

options.A: Giving the patient a written textbook to read silently
options.B: Testing the patient with a written multiple-choice exam
options.C: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words
options.D: Demonstrating a procedure without speaking a single word

explanation: You nailed it! Teach-back is a simple way to confirm the patient truly understood what you explained.

question: A patient feels nervous and ashamed talking about past sexual partners during a clinic visit. What is the best way to handle this as a nurse?

options.A: Scold the patient for engaging in risky behaviors that threaten health
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to build trust and offer education
options.C: Refuse to discuss the topic further until a physician enters the room
options.D: Document the behavior as non-compliant in the permanent hospital record

explanation: You're a natural! Creating a safe, warm space builds trust and makes it easy for patients to share and learn. Keep up the daily habit—you're doing great!

question: How do long, slow government approval processes harm a revolving drug fund?

options.A: It forces patients to buy better quality drugs from abroad
options.B: It gives the pharmacy staff extra time to clean the shelves
options.C: It causes pharmaceutical companies to lower their wholesale prices
options.D: Inflation reduces the real purchasing power of the cash while waiting

explanation: Spot on! When approvals drag on for months, prices go up, meaning your saved cash can suddenly buy way fewer drugs than before.

question: How does menu planning directly impact the budget of a food service unit?

options.A: It has no impact whatsoever on the overall kitchen expenses
options.B: It automatically sets the electricity tariff for the entire hospital building
options.C: It dictates the monthly salary of all administrative personnel
options.D: It determines the types of ingredients purchased and the amount of waste generated

explanation: The menu dictates your shopping list, which directly controls how much money you spend and waste.

question: A patient tells you they are a transgender man who is married to a man. What does this demonstrate?

options.A: Gender identity always determines a person's romantic preferences
options.B: Sexual orientation changes automatically after a social transition
options.C: Gender identity and sexual orientation are completely separate concepts
options.D: Transgender individuals cannot experience same-sex attraction

explanation: This scenario highlights that a person's internal sense of gender does not dictate who they are romantically attracted to. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the core focus of the modern field called nutrigenomics?

options.A: How to grow crops without using water
options.B: How to eliminate all fats from human diets
options.C: How to manufacture artificial synthetic vitamins
options.D: How food and nutrients interact with human genes

explanation: Brilliant! Nutrigenomics looks at the cool science of how your unique genetic makeup changes the way your body responds to the food you eat.

question: What is drug antagonism in plain terms?

options.A: Two drugs combine to create a much larger therapeutic effect
options.B: Plasma protein binding sites become overloaded with free drug
options.C: One drug blocks or counteracts the effect of another drug
options.D: Liver enzymes speed up the clearance of both medications

explanation: Imagine two kids fighting over a single chair. Antagonism is when one drug jumps onto a cell receptor and blocks another substance from getting in or working!

question: Which type of inhaler needs a fast, forceful breath from the patient to work properly?

options.A: Metered-dose inhaler
options.B: Valved holding chamber
options.C: Dry powder inhaler
options.D: Standard nebulizer

explanation: Dry powder inhalers don't use a spray propellant. Instead, the patient's own quick, deep breath pulls the powder out and breaks it up so it can reach the lungs!

question: Which breathing pattern features deep, fast breaths followed by a temporary pause in breathing?

options.A: Biot respiration
options.B: Apneustic breathing
options.C: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
options.D: Kussmaul breathing

explanation: Cheyne-Stokes breathing has regular cycles of breaths getting deeper and faster, then slowing down into a short pause (apnea). It's very common near the end of life.

question: Which injection is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn from tetanus?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.C: Iron and folic acid tablets
options.D: Antimalarial drugs

explanation: Wonderful! Giving the tetanus toxoid vaccine to pregnant women helps build immunity that passes straight to the baby, keeping neonatal tetanus away.

question: Which hormone has a sudden massive surge in the middle of the cycle to trigger ovulation?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: That famous 'LH surge' acts like the starting pistol, signaling the mature egg to pop out of the ovary. Beautiful teamwork by the endocrine system!

question: What is the main goal of using clot-busting (thrombolytic) therapy in an acute ischemic stroke?

options.A: To prevent future heart attacks from occurring
options.B: To dissolve the blood clot and restore blood flow
options.C: To lower systemic blood pressure instantly
options.D: To shrink swollen brain tissue caused by edema

explanation: You got it! Thrombolytic therapy breaks down the clot blocking the vessel, getting oxygen flowing back to starving brain cells quickly.

question: A clinic finds 20 people with malaria in a town of 4,000 residents. What is the prevalence per 1,000 people?
explanation: Divide 20 by 4,000 to get 0.005, then multiply by 1,000 to get 5 per 1,000 people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the main goal of 'pharmacovigilance' in healthcare?

options.A: To speed up the manufacturing process of experimental drugs
options.B: To advertise new pharmaceutical products to doctors and nurses
options.C: To lower the financial cost of purchasing new prescription medicines
options.D: To monitor and report adverse drug effects to improve patient safety

explanation: Pharmacovigilance is just a fancy word for watching out for drug safety. It's all about tracking bad reactions so we can keep patients safe everywhere.

question: What does a person's gender identity refer to?

options.A: Their physical body parts and biological makeup
options.B: The sex assigned to them by a doctor at birth
options.C: Their internal sense of self regarding gender
options.D: The physical clothes and makeup they wear daily

explanation: Gender identity is deeply internal and refers to how a person feels inside about their own gender, rather than their physical appearance or birth assignment. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why do pregnant women often develop swollen ankles and feet by the end of the day?

options.A: Arterial pressure in the legs drops to zero when sitting down.
options.B: Kidneys stop filtering water entirely during the third trimester.
options.C: The bones in the feet expand to make room for extra weight.
options.D: The growing uterus slows down blood return from the lower legs.

explanation: Pressure from the heavy uterus on the large blood vessels in the abdomen slows down blood flow coming back up from the legs, causing fluid to pool in the feet.

question: Which segment of the renal tubule comes immediately after Bowman's capsule?

options.A: Distal convoluted tubule
options.B: Proximal convoluted tubule
options.C: Collecting duct
options.D: Loop of Henle

explanation: The filtered fluid flows directly from Bowman's capsule into the proximal convoluted tubule for massive early reabsorption. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is quick-freezing generally better for food quality than slow freezing?

options.A: It changes the food into a warm, cooked meal instantly
options.B: It forms tiny ice crystals that protect the food's cellular structure
options.C: It completely removes the need for any electricity or freezers
options.D: It adds extra sodium to keep the food tender

explanation: Quick-freezing prevents giant, sharp ice crystals from forming, meaning the delicate cell walls of the food stay intact and taste better later!

question: Why is using misoprostol by itself very common in areas with limited healthcare resources?

options.A: It is widely available, affordable, and effective on its own
options.B: It completely prevents all normal cramping and heavy bleeding
options.C: It removes the need for any follow-up care
options.D: It works twice as fast as other drug combos

explanation: Because mifepristone is hard to get in many places, using misoprostol alone provides a practical and accessible option for safe care. Great job!

question: How do grief and mourning differ from each other?

options.A: Grief is a medical diagnosis, while mourning is a nursing intervention
options.B: Grief only happens in hospitals, while mourning happens at home
options.C: Grief is the internal emotional feeling, while mourning is the outward expression
options.D: Grief lasts for years, while mourning ends after a few days

explanation: Think of grief as what happens inside your heart and mind, while mourning is how you show it on the outside through cultural or religious practices.

question: What is a unique, tell-tale sign of fat embolism syndrome that sets it apart from other types of shock?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both lower extremities
options.B: Swelling of the fingers on the uninjured hand
options.C: A pinpoint petechiae rash across the chest and neck
options.D: A sudden drop in core body temperature

explanation: That distinctive pinprick red-purple rash (petechiae) on the chest and neck is a classic hallmark of fat emboli blocking tiny skin capillaries.

question: What is the heart of reproductive rights?

options.A: The mandatory requirement for every adult to have children
options.B: Free cosmetic surgeries for all citizens reaching adulthood
options.C: Bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion in health decisions
options.D: Government control over family size and birth intervals

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive rights mean every person has the right to make their own free choices about their body and family planning.

question: How do we calculate the pentavalent dropout rate at a primary health clinic?

options.A: Comparing measles vaccine uptake with the number of newborn babies
options.B: Subtracting total children immunized from the total birth population
options.C: Comparing pentavalent dose 1 numbers with pentavalent dose 3 numbers
options.D: Dividing total vaccine doses administered by the number of clinic days

explanation: We find the dropout rate by comparing how many babies took the first dose versus how many actually made it back for the third dose.

question: Which variable always goes on the bottom (horizontal X-axis) of a scatter diagram?

options.A: The average median score
options.B: The dependent outcome
options.C: The independent variable
options.D: The total patient count

explanation: Remember: the independent (or explanatory) variable always sits comfortably on the horizontal X-axis.

question: What causes the nausea and abdominal discomfort many clients feel right after drinking the GTT solution?

options.A: The solution is highly acidic and burns the lining of the esophagus
options.B: The high concentration of sugar creates an osmotic effect in the stomach and gut
options.C: Drinking cold liquid too quickly triggers an involuntary muscle spasm
options.D: The drink contains toxic chemical preservatives that irritate the liver

explanation: A hypertonic sugar drink draws water into the gastrointestinal tract through osmosis, often causing cramping, nausea, and bloating. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h8)

question: Why must you clean connection hubs with an alcohol swab before changing lines?

options.A: It ensures the plastic tubing remains soft and flexible
options.B: It makes the digital screen easier to read in bright light
options.C: It removes sticky residue left behind by medical tape
options.D: It prevents microbes from entering the bloodstream and causing infection

explanation: Spot on! Good aseptic technique keeps nasty bacteria from hitching a ride directly into your patient's bloodstream.

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.A: Complete disappearance of capillary beds
options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.C: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged valves
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults.

question: Which tiny bumps on the tongue do NOT contain any taste buds?

options.A: Filiform papillae
options.B: Foliate papillae
options.C: Circumvallate papillae
options.D: Fungiform papillae

explanation: Filiform papillae are the most common bumps on your tongue; they give it a rough texture to help move food around, but they do not have taste buds.

question: When would you choose an intramuscular injection instead of giving pills by mouth?

options.A: When the patient cannot take oral medications
options.B: When the patient wants to avoid any skin punctures
options.C: When the medication needs to work over a full week
options.D: When the drug is completely harmless to the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is vomiting or unable to swallow, going through the muscle is a safe and reliable backup plan. Keep up the good work!

question: Who usually acts as the main communication link for the home health team?

options.A: The family pet owner
options.B: The patient's insurance case manager
options.C: The local pharmacist
options.D: The primary home health nurse

explanation: You are the captain of the ship! The primary nurse coordinates visits, gathers updates from other therapists, and updates the doctor.

question: Which specialist should you call to trim the toenails of a patient with advanced diabetic foot complications?

options.A: A general ward nurse
options.B: A physical therapist
options.C: A hospital pharmacist
options.D: A podiatrist

explanation: Spot on! Podiatrists are foot experts trained to safely handle high-risk nail and skin care for patients with poor circulation or nerve issues.

question: Why is a budget considered such an important financial tool?

options.A: It provides a clear benchmark to compare actual spending against planned goals
options.B: It automatically generates profits without requiring staff work
options.C: It gives nurse managers unlimited power to hire any staff they want
options.D: It stops patients from ever questioning their hospital bills

explanation: A budget sets a clear target so managers can check whether the unit is staying on track or spending too much.

question: What happens in the chest when your diaphragm contracts during a breath in?

options.A: The pleural space fills entirely with air
options.B: Positive pressure forces air out of the lungs
options.C: Negative pressure is created to pull air in
options.D: Pressure inside the chest equals atmospheric pressure

explanation: When the diaphragm moves down, it opens up space and lowers the pressure inside, drawing air naturally into your lungs. Beautiful concept to master!

question: What should be the main focus during an MBO performance review meeting?

options.A: Reducing the number of nursing staff on duty
options.B: Debating political topics outside of healthcare
options.C: Finding someone to blame when targets are missed
options.D: Problem-solving and comparing results with original goals

explanation: MBO reviews focus on comparing actual outcomes to set objectives and solving any problems that hindered success. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why is feeling the uterus during a physical assessment so important when suspecting postpartum endometritis?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the organ
options.B: To check for tenderness and a boggy texture
options.C: To test the strength of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: To evaluate the size of the ovaries

explanation: A healthy postpartum uterus should feel firm as it shrinks back down. An infected one feels tender and soft, or 'boggy,' because it's struggling to contract.

question: How does a functional drug classification differ from a therapeutic one?

options.A: It focuses strictly on the financial cost of the medication
options.B: It describes how the drug works at a cellular or physiological level
options.C: It dictates the preferred route of administration for the nurse
options.D: It lists only the herbal ingredients found in traditional remedies

explanation: While therapeutic class tells you the disease treated, functional class explains the exact body process or cellular mechanism the drug alters.

question: What should you do immediately if mixed medications inside a syringe driver turn cloudy?

options.A: Vigorously shake the syringe to dissolve the cloudy particles back in
options.B: Leave the pump running because color changes are completely normal
options.C: Increase the infusion rate to push the cloudy solution through faster
options.D: Discard the mixture immediately because the drugs are likely incompatible

explanation: Well done! Cloudiness means a chemical reaction happened between the drugs, making them unsafe. Never give a cloudy mixture—always prepare a fresh, safe set.

question: On an ECG machine, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.A: The heart resting and recovering
options.B: Upper chambers squeezing
options.C: Lower chambers relaxing
options.D: Lower chambers electrical activity before they squeeze

explanation: The big tall spike on the ECG screen (the QRS) is the electrical wave racing through the ventricles right before they pump blood out.

question: Why do you pull the skin taut instead of pinching it before an intradermal injection?

options.A: Taut skin makes the needle sharper as it enters
options.B: Pinching causes severe bruising around the injection site
options.C: Pinching the skin lifts it and accidentally creates a subcutaneous pocket
options.D: Pulling the skin taut numbs the nerve endings temporarily

explanation: Well done! Pinching bunches up the fatty layer underneath, making it way too easy to accidentally slide past the dermis.

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

options.A: A simple reaction to eating too much sugar
options.B: Signs of potential pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Normal physiological changes due to increased sleep
options.D: Standard fatigue that requires drinking more coffee

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined in pregnancy are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Grab that BP cuff right away!

question: What is the best position for a patient during an abdominal paracentesis?

options.A: Flat on the back in a supine position
options.B: In a steep Trendelenburg position
options.C: Lying completely flat on the stomach
options.D: Sitting upright or semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting up lets gravity pull the fluid down to the lower belly, making it much easier and safer for the doctor to reach.

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient gets a chemical splash in their eye?

options.A: Put in neutralizing acid drops to balance the pH
options.B: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop spreading
options.C: Cover the eye with a dry cotton pad and wait
options.D: Flush the eye continuously with clean water or saline for 15 to 30 minutes

explanation: Time is everything with chemical splashes! Wash it out immediately with lots of clean water or saline to protect the cornea from lasting damage.

question: How do healthy lifestyle habits primarily help men dealing with mild andropause symptoms?

options.A: By stopping the liver from producing binding proteins
options.B: By improving body composition, energy levels, and mood
options.C: By entirely replacing the need for medical check-ups
options.D: By permanently reversing the decline of testicular hormone production

explanation: While lifestyle changes won't stop natural aging or hormone drops, eating well and exercising work wonders for boosting energy and keeping spirits high!

question: Which major complication do rehabilitation nurses constantly work to prevent?

options.A: Sudden visual impairment
options.B: Spontaneous bone fractures
options.C: Acute myocardial infarction
options.D: Pressure injuries and contractures

explanation: Great job! Because rehab patients often spend a lot of time resting, nurses watch closely to prevent bed sores (pressure injuries) and stiff joints (contractures).

question: What is the primary purpose of barrier nursing?

options.A: To completely cure chronic infectious diseases
options.B: To stop pathogens from spreading between people
options.C: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.D: To replace the need for routine handwashing

explanation: Barrier nursing uses physical blocks to prevent germs from moving from one person or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: During which gestational weeks is a routine GTT typically performed for pregnant women?

options.A: Between 24 and 28 weeks
options.B: Between 8 and 12 weeks
options.C: Between 32 and 36 weeks
options.D: Immediately upon discovering the pregnancy

explanation: Gestational diabetes screening via GTT is standard practice during the late second trimester when placental hormones peak. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h2)

question: What is a very common physical reason why clients stop using their family planning method?

options.A: Gaining the ability to read medical textbooks
options.B: Complete recovery from all chronic illnesses
options.C: Experiencing troublesome side effects like irregular bleeding
options.D: Developing an allergy to clinic waiting room chairs

explanation: Unmanaged side effects are a primary reason clients stop their method. A quick counseling chat about what to expect can make all the difference!

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for respiratory complications in the ICU?

options.A: Eating a high-protein hospital diet
options.B: Mechanical ventilation and artificial airways
options.C: Having normal blood pressure readings
options.D: Walking in the hallway twice a day

explanation: Artificial airways and mechanical ventilators bypass normal body defenses, making it much easier for bacteria to cause pneumonia and for lung tissue to collapse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h2)

question: What hormone stimulates the gallbladder to contract and release bile into the small intestine?

options.A: Secretin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cholecystokinin (CCK)
options.D: Gastrin

explanation: CCK is released in response to dietary fats and proteins, causing the gallbladder to release stored bile. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical behavioral warning sign of an eating disorder in a teenager?

options.A: Obsessive preoccupation with calorie counting and food labels
options.B: Eating large balanced meals happily with family every evening
options.C: Wearing oversized clothing to hide noticeable weight loss
options.D: Frequent trips to the bathroom immediately following meals

explanation: Spot on! Teens with eating disorders usually avoid family dinners or hide their eating habits, rather than happily enjoying big meals with everyone.

question: What is the main action the male partner must take during the withdrawal method?

options.A: Taking an oral herbal tea before sexual activity
options.B: Washing the genital area immediately after intercourse
options.C: Pulling the penis out of the vagina before ejaculation
options.D: Wearing a thin latex sheath throughout intercourse

explanation: Withdrawal is all about timing: the man must remove his penis from the vaginal canal completely before releasing any semen.

question: Why are progestin-only pills usually recommended for breastfeeding mothers instead of combined oral pills?

options.A: They provide permanent protection after a single dose
options.B: They do not interfere with breast milk production
options.C: They completely stop all menstrual bleeding forever
options.D: They protect the mother against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Since progestin-only pills don't have estrogen, they keep a mother's milk supply safe and flowing for her baby. Brilliant clinical reasoning!

question: Why is the briefing phase right before a scenario so important for students?

options.A: It gives students time to memorize a script for the patient interaction
options.B: It allows the instructor to test students on random trivia questions
options.C: It ensures that no student is ever allowed to make a clinical mistake
options.D: It establishes ground rules and helps create a safe psychological space

explanation: The briefing clarifies the rules, explains the environment, and reassures students so they feel comfortable participating without fear. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which healthcare professional is an expert at helping a stroke patient relearn how to swallow and speak?

options.A: Clinical dietitian
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Hospital social worker

explanation: Speech-language pathologists are wonderful allies who specialize in helping patients recover their communication and safe swallowing skills after a brain injury.

question: What does 'full cost recovery' mean when pricing drugs in a DRF?

options.A: Recovering the purchase price plus all operational expenses needed to supply the drug
options.B: Selling the drugs at the exact same price the manufacturer printed on the box
options.C: Charging double the market price to make a large profit for the clinic
options.D: Waiting for the government to refund the pharmacy after all drugs are sold out

explanation: It simply means the price covers not just what the supplier charged, but also the extra costs of bringing the medicine safely to the pharmacy.

question: What is the primary public health way to prevent iodine deficiency in a population?

options.A: Providing Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food packets
options.B: Distributing high-dose vitamin A capsules
options.C: Promoting the universal use of iodized salt
options.D: Administering iron-folate tablets to infants

explanation: Correct! Iodized salt is the simplest, most effective way to reach everyone and stop conditions like goiter from developing.

question: What is the main reason healthcare providers use drug classification systems?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for doctor prescriptions
options.B: To help nurses administer medications safely and anticipate effects
options.C: To ensure all medications cost the same amount of money
options.D: To make drug manufacturing companies produce fewer pills

explanation: Grouping drugs helps nurses predict how a medication will work and watch out for specific side effects during patient care. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the best test to confirm the exact bilirubin level in a newborn?

options.A: Transcutaneous skin scanner
options.B: Serum bilirubin blood test
options.C: Urine color comparison chart
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: While skin scanners are quick, a blood test gives the exact measurement the doctor needs to decide if phototherapy is necessary.

question: Why might a bright, gifted child suddenly get poor grades on school tests?

options.A: A preference for learning physical skills over reading
options.B: An inability to process spoken instructions in class
options.C: Boredom from a lack of appropriate mental challenge
options.D: Severe physical fatigue caused by rapid growth spurts

explanation: It sounds surprising, but when schoolwork isn't challenging enough, brilliant kids get bored and check out. You're building solid nursing intuition!

question: What should you do if a laboring woman's cervical dilation line crosses the action line on the partograph?

options.A: Waiting another four hours to see if contractions naturally pick up speed
options.B: Discharging the patient home to walk around until contractions become stronger
options.C: Stopping all forms of monitoring and allowing the patient to sleep undisturbed
options.D: Immediate medical intervention and preparation for emergency transfer or surgery

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is not progressing normally. It is your cue to call for backup and get ready for urgent help or a C-section.

question: What does scientific empiricism primarily rely on for gathering medical knowledge?

options.A: Strict adherence to ancient religious texts
options.B: Careful observation and physical experimentation
options.C: Interpreting dreams and spiritual visions
options.D: Blind trust in traditional folklore

explanation: Empiricism values tangible evidence gained through direct observation, testing, and experimentation rather than accepting claims based on tradition or authority alone. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is a very normal emotional reaction for patients waiting to find out if they have cancer?

options.A: Uncontrolled physical hunger
options.B: Extreme happiness and relief
options.C: Intense anxiety and shock
options.D: Complete emotional numbness

explanation: Waiting for big health news is terrifying. Shock and heavy anxiety are very common reactions that nurses need to be ready to support.

question: Where do the main coronary arteries start from?

options.A: The left ventricle
options.B: The superior vena cava
options.C: The ascending aorta
options.D: The pulmonary artery

explanation: Great job! The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the ascending aorta, just above the aortic valve, so they can grab freshly oxygenated blood first thing.

question: What does a psychologically safe nursing classroom help students do?

options.A: Ignore hospital safety guidelines during patient care
options.B: Pass all nursing board examinations without studying
options.C: Skip difficult clinical shifts without facing any penalties
options.D: Admit what they do not know without fear of harsh judgment

explanation: When you feel safe, you can freely speak up about mistakes or confusion without being judged. That openness is key to keeping patients safe in the clinic!

question: What type of data is best displayed using a bar chart?

options.A: Individual patient DNA sequences
options.B: Raw unorganized audio
options.C: Categorical data
options.D: Continuous time data

explanation: Bar charts are specifically designed to show and compare distinct groups or categories of information. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h1)

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

options.A: Frequent requests for promotion and salary increases
options.B: Sudden weight loss, hair discoloration, and chronic joint pain
options.C: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment
options.D: Excessive enthusiasm, overconfidence, and skipping breaks

explanation: Burnout makes you feel emotionally drained, detached from patients, and like nothing you do makes a difference. Always check on your mental health!

question: A mother cannot afford the expensive imported supplements recommended for her underweight toddler. As her nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Tell her that nutrition counseling is no longer necessary if she cannot afford items
options.B: Help the mother adapt affordable, locally available foods to enrich the child's diet
options.C: Advise her to stop feeding the child solid foods until financial aid arrives
options.D: Insist that she buy the expensive supplements regardless of her financial situation

explanation: Real nursing meets people where they are. Great health education uses accessible, local market foods to make nutritious meals practical for every family.

question: In Nigeria, which official agency is responsible for receiving reports of adverse drug reactions?

options.A: FMOH
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NMA
options.D: NMCN

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our national body that keeps watch over drug safety and collects these reports.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal local reaction to a topical drug?

options.A: Contact dermatitis at the site
options.B: Local burning or stinging
options.C: Anaphylactic shock originating in the lungs
options.D: Pruritus and skin redness

explanation: Anaphylactic shock is a serious whole-body allergic emergency, whereas local reactions only happen right where you applied the cream.

question: Why can a blocked intestine (bowel obstruction) eventually lead to a tear or perforation?

options.A: Trapped pressure cuts off the blood supply to the wall
options.B: The liver swells and crushes the intestines
options.C: Digestive enzymes dissolve the outside of the skin
options.D: Patients eat too much roughage while blocked

explanation: You nailed it! As contents pile up behind a blockage, the pressure squeezes the blood vessels in the intestinal wall until the tissue dies and tears. Physics and anatomy working together!

question: Why are maternity homes so important in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They replace federal tertiary teaching hospitals completely
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medications during labor
options.C: They offer free surgical care funded by international donors
options.D: They serve as local bridges to care when distant hospitals are hard to reach

explanation: Spot on! By being close by, they bridge the gap so mums don't have to travel huge distances just to get basic care.

question: Which patient condition means Oral Rehydration Therapy is unsafe, requiring IV fluids instead?

options.A: Mild watery diarrhea with normal skin turgor
options.B: Profound hypovolemic shock with altered consciousness
options.C: Low-grade fever and mild nausea
options.D: Frequent loose stools without vomiting

explanation: If a patient is in shock or unconscious, they cannot swallow safely. They need quick intravenous fluids to restore their blood pressure.

question: Why can steroid hormones slip right out of cells as soon as they are made?

options.A: They are pushed out by water pressure inside the cytoplasm
options.B: They are small enough to pass through active transport protein pumps
options.C: They are stored in large vesicles that burst open upon stimulation
options.D: They are fat-soluble and can cross lipid cell membranes easily

explanation: Because cell membranes are also made of fats (lipids), fat-loving steroid hormones pass straight through them like an open door—no special channels needed!

question: What is the primary goal of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To give the doctor time to finish other ward rounds
options.B: To test the patient's memory and cognitive function
options.C: To reduce anxiety and help them adjust to the new environment
options.D: To ensure the patient fills out their discharge papers early

explanation: A good orientation helps a frightened or stressed patient feel secure by showing them how things work around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended way to reduce the spread of STIs in men?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic use to boost natural immunity
options.B: Participating in routine periodic screening tests
options.C: Ensuring prompt treatment of all identified sexual partners
options.D: Consistent and correct use of latex barrier condoms

explanation: Stopping antibiotics is a huge no-no! It leads to treatment failure and superbugs, not immunity.

question: What is the main purpose of reviewing past adverse events and near misses in a hospital unit?

options.A: To find a specific staff member to blame for the mistake
options.B: To refine safety protocols and improve future patient care
options.C: To increase the cost of patient hospital bills
options.D: To reduce the number of shifts nurses have to work

explanation: Quality improvement treats mistakes and close calls as learning opportunities to fix broken systems rather than punish individuals. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the difference between withholding and withdrawing medical treatment?

options.A: Withholding is illegal, while withdrawing is legally permitted
options.B: There is no difference in definition, only in the cost of medications
options.C: Withholding requires court approval, while withdrawing requires only family consent
options.D: Withholding means never starting an intervention, while withdrawing means stopping an ongoing one

explanation: It's all about timing! Withholding means you decide not to start a treatment in the first place, while withdrawing means you turn off or stop a treatment that was already running.

question: After a very tough shift, which activity helps a nurse process their emotions and learn from the experience?

options.A: Ignoring the incident
options.B: Reflective journaling
options.C: Changing clinical wards
options.D: Filing an incident report

explanation: Writing down your thoughts in a reflective journal is a great way to unwind, process tough moments, and grow into a stronger nurse.

question: Which professional does the home health nurse frequently collaborate with to improve patient mobility?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Biomedical engineer
options.D: Hospital pharmacist

explanation: Physical therapists work closely with home health nurses to help patients regain strength, balance, and safe movement at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why must a nurse always make sure a water-soluble lubricant is used for a proctoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the light source from overheating inside the rectum
options.B: To sterilize the metal components of privacy equipment instantly
options.C: To act as a strong local anesthetic agent for the rectal walls
options.D: To ease smooth passage through the anal sphincter without harming tissue

explanation: Great choice! Water-soluble jelly reduces friction so the scope slides in comfortably without hurting the patient, and it washes away easily afterward.

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?

options.A: 31 pairs
options.B: 24 pairs
options.C: 12 pairs
options.D: 8 pairs

explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves that connect the brain directly to various structures mostly located in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which quick screening tool is specifically designed to check for substance use risks in teenagers?

options.A: Braden scale
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: CRAFFT questionnaire
options.D: Apgar score

explanation: Brilliant! The CRAFFT is a short, friendly screening tool specially built to spot substance-related risks in adolescents.

question: What happens right away when a bone gets fractured?

options.A: Immediate hardening of a permanent bony callus
options.B: Rapid degradation of surrounding articular cartilage
options.C: Instant conversion of osteoblasts into osteoclasts
options.D: Formation of a blood clot or fracture hematoma

explanation: When a bone breaks, blood vessels tear, and blood pools around the area to form a protective clot (hematoma) to kick off healing.

question: Why are good learning experiences so important for you as a nursing student?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any written nursing examinations
options.B: They help connect classroom theory to real patient care realities
options.C: They shorten the overall duration of the nursing training program
options.D: They guarantee that students never make clinical errors on the ward

explanation: They bridge the gap between what you read in your textbooks and what you actually see and do at the bedside. Great for building your confidence!

question: A public health team rushes to a village to investigate a sudden outbreak of measles only. What type of assessment are they doing?

options.A: Problem-oriented community diagnosis
options.B: National census data collection
options.C: Hospital morbidity survey
options.D: Comprehensive community diagnosis

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! When we zero in on one specific issue or outbreak instead of looking at the whole community, we call it a problem-oriented approach.

question: When you digest carbohydrates, what is the main sugar that enters your bloodstream?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Glycerol
options.D: Glycogen

explanation: Glucose is the star player here! It is the primary, easy-to-use sugar that our bodies and brains love to burn for quick energy.

question: When you tell a patient the 'indication' of a drug, what are you actually explaining to them?

options.A: To help the nurse calculate the correct financial cost of the prescription
options.B: To teach the patient the chemical formula of the active ingredient
options.C: To determine how quickly the drug will be eliminated by the kidneys
options.D: To ensure the patient knows the therapeutic purpose of the treatment

explanation: An 'indication' just means the reason for taking the drug—what illness or symptom it is meant to fix. Simple as that!

question: A nurse in a state that hasn't domesticated the VAPP act suspects a young girl is about to undergo FGM. What is the biggest hurdle the nurse faces?

options.A: Being forced by law to assist with the procedure
options.B: A federal rule banning police involvement in local matters
options.C: Getting fired from the nursing council for reporting abuse
options.D: Not having clear local laws or penalties to punish the perpetrators

explanation: Well thought out! Without local laws criminalizing FGM, police officers lack the legal backing to arrest perpetrators or intervene effectively before it happens.

question: Which alternative exit route for drugs is especially important for nurses to remember when caring for breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: Mammary excretion
options.B: Sweat gland secretion
options.C: Salivary elimination
options.D: Pulmonary excretion

explanation: Drugs can pass into breast milk through the mammary glands. As nurses, we always check if a mother's medications are safe for her breastfeeding infant!

question: What happens to the total drug effect during synergism?

options.A: It drops lower than the effect of either single drug
options.B: It equals the exact sum of both individual effects
options.C: It becomes greater than the sum of the individual effects
options.D: It completely cancels out any therapeutic benefit

explanation: Think of synergism like teamwork! When two drugs work together synergistically, their combined power is much greater than what each could ever do on its own.

question: Imagine a nurse is testing a new handwashing technique and makes sure every ward uses the exact same water temperature and soap brand. Why do this?

options.A: To punish wards that do not follow hospital rules
options.B: To prove that water temperature is the only cause of illness
options.C: To control outside variables that could affect infection rates
options.D: To save money on purchasing hospital cleaning supplies

explanation: Exactly right! By keeping things like water and soap the same, you make sure any change in infection rates is truly because of the new technique, not random outside factors.

question: Why is supporting family caregivers considered such a vital part of home healthcare?

options.A: To prevent caregiver burnout and maintain safe care at home
options.B: Because family members replace the doctor in writing prescriptions
options.C: To ensure the family pays for all medical supplies out of pocket
options.D: Because nurses are not allowed to visit patients alone

explanation: Caring for a sick relative is exhausting. By supporting family caregivers, we protect their health and ensure they can keep providing safe care at home.

question: Which type of nerve fibers send those sharp, instant pain signals?

options.A: Ruffini fibers
options.B: Merkel fibers
options.C: C fibers
options.D: A-delta fibers

explanation: Brilliant! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin, which lets them rush electrical impulses quickly to cause that sharp first pain.

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a public hospital?

options.A: To fund free medical care for all citizens indefinitely
options.B: To generate large commercial profits for hospital expansion
options.C: To replace the national health ministry budget entirely
options.D: To guarantee a steady, continuous supply of essential medicines

explanation: Spot on! The whole point of a DRF is to make sure the pharmacy never runs out of crucial drugs by using a self-replenishing pool of money.

question: Which of these is NOT a correct way to handle hospital waste?

options.A: Sealing biohazard bags securely before carrying them out
options.B: Disposing of sharp needles in designated puncture-proof boxes
options.C: Leaving overfilled waste bags open in the hallway
options.D: Wearing gloves when touching soiled linen or dressings

explanation: Leaving dirty waste bags open in public view is a major hazard! Always seal and dispose of waste safely.

question: When smooth muscles in the penis relax, what happens to the helical arteries?

options.A: They redirect all blood flow exclusively to the urethra
options.B: They dilate to allow a massive surge of blood into the sinusoids
options.C: They collapse entirely to prevent any further fluid entry
options.D: They constrict to trap the blood already inside the chambers

explanation: Spot on! Relaxing the muscle walls lets the arteries open wide, flooding the tissue spaces with blood.

question: What is a major challenge when conducting a longitudinal study in nursing research?

options.A: Higher risk of manipulating the independent variable by accident
options.B: Inability to ever observe changes over time
options.C: Participants dropping out over time, leading to missing data
options.D: Results are always available immediately within days

explanation: Spot on! Following people for months or years is tough because participants sometimes move away, lose interest, or drop out, which researchers call attrition.

question: What does the abbreviation 'PO' mean on a drug chart?

options.A: By rectum
options.B: By mouth
options.C: Intravenously
options.D: Under the tongue

explanation: Well done! 'PO' stands for 'per os', a Latin phrase meaning by mouth. It's one of the most common routes you'll administer medications.

question: What is another common term used to describe a brand name drug?

options.A: Generic identifier
options.B: Chemical name
options.C: Universal formula
options.D: Proprietary name

explanation: A brand name is also called a proprietary name because the company 'properly' owns the rights to that specific marketing title.

question: What is the normal resting heart rate range for a healthy adult?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 140 beats per minute
options.C: 40 to 60 beats per minute
options.D: 100 to 120 beats per minute

explanation: You've got this! A healthy adult's heart normally beats between 60 and 100 times per minute while resting. This keeps enough blood flowing to all parts of the body.

question: When should you as a nurse switch to surgical asepsis instead of medical asepsis?

options.A: Before giving oral medication to a patient in the general ward
options.B: During any procedure that enters a normally sterile body cavity
options.C: After finishing a routine bed bath for an adult patient
options.D: Whenever entering a patient room with a known respiratory infection

explanation: You're doing great! Whenever we do invasive things like passing a catheter or assisting in theater, we need total sterility to protect deep body tissues from infection.

question: Which lab finding is a well-known kidney side effect of long-term D-penicillamine use?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Proteinuria
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Hyperbilirubinemia

explanation: Thiol drugs can sometimes irritate the delicate filtering units of the kidneys, causing protein to leak into the urine (proteinuria). Regular checks keep patients safe!

question: Which of these is a key feature of passive immunization?

options.A: It takes several weeks to start working
options.B: It stimulates long-lasting immune memory
options.C: It uses live, virulent disease strains
options.D: It provides immediate but temporary protection

explanation: Passive immunity is like borrowing an umbrella—you get instant protection when you need it, but it doesn't last forever because your body didn't make the memory cells.

question: If a patient taking a thioamide medication reports which symptom, should you suspect a serious blood issue like agranulocytosis?

options.A: Slight tremors in fingers
options.B: Mild nausea after meals
options.C: Fever and sore throat
options.D: Dry skin and constipation

explanation: Always take a new fever and sore throat seriously with these meds; it can be an early warning sign of a dangerously low white blood cell count.

question: What is the main advantage of an interprofessional healthcare team for an elderly patient?

options.A: Lower overall healthcare costs for the government
options.B: Comprehensive care that improves overall quality of life
options.C: Faster discharge from acute care hospitals
options.D: Elimination of the need for informal family caregivers

explanation: When different health professionals combine their skills, all aspects of the patient's physical, emotional, and social needs get covered, leading to happier, healthier days.

question: What is a normal, expected sensation for a patient receiving intravenous contrast dye during a CT scan?

options.A: A sharp, intense pain in the joints
options.B: Sudden numbness in both lower legs
options.C: Extreme drowsiness and deep sleep
options.D: A warm flushing feeling over the body

explanation: As the iodinated contrast enters the bloodstream, patients frequently report a sudden wave of body warmth, a metallic taste, or a warm sensation near the bladder. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h4)

question: What condition involves widespread, abnormal blood clotting followed by severe bleeding due to used-up clotting factors?

options.A: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
options.D: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

explanation: DIC is a serious complication where small clots form throughout the body, eventually exhausting clotting proteins and causing severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is delegation such a helpful skill for nurses on a busy ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to manage workload by sharing routine care tasks safely
options.B: It prevents junior staff from learning advanced clinical procedures
options.C: It eliminates the need for any direct patient assessment by the nurse
options.D: It completely removes nursing liability from ward management

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing the buck; it's about teamwork! It helps spread out daily care duties so every patient gets timely attention.

question: What is the medical term for when an erection goes away and the penis returns to a soft state?

options.A: Tumescence
options.B: Detumescence
options.C: Vasodilation
options.D: Priapism

explanation: Keep learning! Detumescence simply means the easing of an erection back to normal, soft tissue.

question: If a patient has a large left-sided tension pneumothorax, which way is the trachea likely to shift?

options.A: Tracheal deviation toward the left side
options.B: Downward displacement of the liver
options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the right side
options.D: No movement of the mediastinal structures

explanation: Think of it like a crowded room: pressure builds up on the left and pushes everything over toward the healthy right side. You're building solid emergency nursing instincts!

question: Why do intramuscular injections get absorbed faster than subcutaneous ones?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat contains no blood vessels
options.B: Muscles produce enzymes that break down drugs
options.C: The needle used is always much thinner
options.D: Muscle tissue has a rich blood supply

explanation: Great job thinking about how drugs move in the body! Muscles have plenty of blood vessels, which helps medications rush quickly into the bloodstream. You've got this!

question: Why do the cells in our body constantly need blood flowing to them?

options.A: To produce white blood cells directly inside the tissue spaces
options.B: To keep blood pressure at zero in the outer extremities
options.C: To deliver oxygen and nutrients while removing waste products
options.D: To cool down the internal organs by releasing sweat locally

explanation: Think of blood as the body's ultimate delivery and sanitation service! Cells need a steady supply of oxygen and food to survive, and they produce waste that must be carried away.

question: What is another common name for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Cerebral shunt
options.B: Spinal tap
options.C: Epidural injection
options.D: Bone marrow biopsy

explanation: A lumbar puncture is commonly referred to as a spinal tap because it involves accessing fluid from the spinal column. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why must nurses monitor vital signs very closely when a patient is going through alcohol withdrawal?

options.A: It ensures the patient stays awake during visiting hours
options.B: It helps the patient lose weight faster during hospitalization
options.C: Severe withdrawal can cause dangerous spikes in blood pressure and seizures
options.D: It is required to calculate the exact hospital bill total

explanation: Alcohol withdrawal can be very dangerous, triggering severe tremors, high blood pressure, and seizures. Careful monitoring saves lives!

question: Blood pooling in the legs from long-term bed rest can lead to which major vascular complication?

options.A: Essential hypertension
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
options.C: Coronary artery disease
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: When movement stops, blood slows down in the legs and can form clots. That's why early ambulation and leg exercises are so important in nursing care!

question: Which of these is a clear example of objective data?

options.A: A feeling of dizziness upon standing up quickly
options.B: A body temperature reading of 38.5 degrees Celsius
options.C: A statement of anxiety about upcoming surgery
options.D: A patient reporting a dull ache in the lower back

explanation: Objective data is what you can actually see, touch, or measure yourself (like a thermometer reading), unlike feelings that only the patient can tell you about.

question: What is the most common and clear sign that a patient has a kidney injury?

options.A: Severe swelling of both legs
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Inability to pass any stool
options.D: Blood in the urine

explanation: Seeing blood in the urine (medical name: hematuria) is the classic red flag that tells us the kidneys have taken a hit. Always watch out for this in trauma cases!

question: Which of these is NOT strictly needed for normal blood flow to body tissues?

options.A: A healthy and effective cardiac pump
options.B: Sufficient circulating blood volume
options.C: Normal functioning of the liver and spleen
options.D: An intact and open blood vessel network

explanation: While your liver and spleen do amazing filter work, the absolute basics needed for body perfusion are just a pump (the heart), pipes (blood vessels), and fluid volume!

question: Why do people easily fall for popular food trends?

options.A: Scientific journals publish strict guidelines endorsing them.
options.B: These trends offer appealing quick fixes for body image and wellness goals.
options.C: Hospitals and clinics mandate these diets for all new admissions.
options.D: Nutritional fads are always cheaper than buying regular food items.

explanation: Everyone loves a shortcut! When a diet promises fast, easy results, it's hard not to listen. Great job thinking it through.

question: What is the bright triangular light reflex seen on a normal tympanic membrane called?

options.A: The umbo flare
options.B: The malleus reflection
options.C: The annular ring
options.D: The cone of light

explanation: The cone of light is a normal light reflection bouncing off the concave surface of the healthy eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does incidence differ from prevalence in community health data?

options.A: Incidence counts deaths, while prevalence counts active infections
options.B: Incidence is calculated yearly, while prevalence is calculated daily
options.C: Incidence measures new cases over time, while prevalence measures total existing cases
options.D: Incidence only applies to children, while prevalence applies to adults

explanation: Incidence tracks how fast a disease is spreading by counting new cases, whereas prevalence shows how widespread a condition currently is within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do we track a child's growth over several visits rather than relying on just one measurement?

options.A: It prevents errors made by community health volunteers
options.B: It shows the direction and velocity of growth over time
options.C: It guarantees the child will not contract infectious diseases
options.D: It is required by government health insurance policies

explanation: A single visit only tells you about today. Tracking over time shows the true pattern—whether the child is growing well or falling behind.

question: How do the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) differ from the earlier selective health approaches?

options.A: They rely only on private hospitals instead of community clinics
options.B: They focus exclusively on curing adult heart disease in wealthy nations
options.C: They completely ignore maternal and child health in favor of space research
options.D: They return to a broader, more comprehensive vision of health linked to overall development

explanation: SDG 3 and related goals embrace a wide-ranging view of health and well-being, echoing the holistic spirit of the original Alma-Ata declaration. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: In nursing and science, what does 'pH' stand for?

options.A: Power of hydration
options.B: Pressure of homeostasis
options.C: Potential of hydrogen
options.D: Percentage of hydroxyl

explanation: pH simply stands for the 'potential of hydrogen'. It tells us how many free hydrogen ions are floating around in a fluid, which determines how acidic or basic it is!

question: What is the best way to assess a toddler's neurological function during a physical exam?

options.A: Observe their spontaneous play and developmental milestones
options.B: Ask them to complete a written multiple-choice test
options.C: Keep them completely still and silent for thirty minutes
options.D: Perform a strict formal cranial nerve exam immediately

explanation: Toddlers cannot follow complex commands, so observing natural movement and play provides the best clinical insight. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h7)

question: A conscious patient refuses to take their prescribed medication. What should you do first?

options.A: Threaten to discharge them immediately from the ward
options.B: Crush the drug into their food without telling them
options.C: Force the medication into their mouth for their own good
options.D: Explore their reasons and notify the prescriber

explanation: Patients always have the right to say no. Take a moment to listen to their worries and let the doctor know, rather than forcing anything.

question: What happens if a nurse forgets to push the foreskin back down after cleaning an uncircumcised male patient?

options.A: Paraphimosis and painful swelling of the penis
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.C: Total blockage of urine flow
options.D: A fast fungal infection on the legs

explanation: Spot on! Leaving the foreskin pulled back acts like a tight rope, cutting off blood flow and causing a painful swelling called paraphimosis.

question: When a patient needs both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, why should the bronchodilator be used first?

options.A: It stops the side effects of the steroid from harming the heart
options.B: It neutralizes stomach acid that might interfere with breathing
options.C: It opens the airways so the steroid can reach deeper into the lungs
options.D: It cleans the mouth so the patient does not develop a fungal infection

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first widens the bronchial tubes, allowing the corticosteroid to penetrate further down into the respiratory tree. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which emergency medication should a nurse always keep at the bedside after a parathyroid surgery?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: IV calcium gluconate is your go-to safety net at the bedside to quickly treat sudden, severe low calcium or muscle spasms after neck surgery.

question: A nurse notices many young girls in her area suffering complications from unsafe procedures. What is her best first step?

options.A: Establish youth-friendly education sessions and ensure non-judgmental contraceptive counseling
options.B: Refuse to treat post-abortion complications until community leaders apologize
options.C: Close the primary health clinic and refer all emergency cases to overseas hospitals
options.D: Report all teenagers visiting the clinic to local law enforcement agencies immediately

explanation: Brilliant choice! To fix the root of the problem, we need friendly education and open, supportive family planning care so kids can get help safely.

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for an infectious cervical irritation?

options.A: Eliminating the underlying pathogen with targeted medications
options.B: Numbing the pelvic nerve endings to eliminate pain sensations
options.C: Permanently removing the cervix to stop future infections
options.D: Increasing local hormone production through oral supplements

explanation: You got it! To fix an infection, we find out what germ is causing it and hit it with the right medication.

question: What special mask is a must-have for Airborne Precautions?

options.A: Disposable plastic apron
options.B: Clean non-sterile gloves
options.C: Standard surgical mask
options.D: N95 respirator mask

explanation: Tiny germs floating in the air need an N95 respirator to filter them out before they reach your lungs. Safety first!

question: What's the main difference between 'in situ' breast cancer and 'invasive' breast cancer?

options.A: In situ cancer only affects men, while invasive cancer only affects women
options.B: In situ cancer causes severe pain, while invasive cancer is completely painless
options.C: In situ cancer stays confined within the ducts, while invasive cancer spreads to surrounding tissue
options.D: In situ cancer requires chemotherapy, while invasive cancer requires no treatment

explanation: In situ means 'in its place'—it hasn't broken out of the duct yet. Once it breaks through, it's invasive and can travel.

question: What medication is immediately required if a patient experiences a severe anaphylactic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Metformin
options.C: Aspirin
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving first-line drug used to treat severe allergic reactions, opening airways and supporting blood pressure. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the main goal of primary health care in our communities?

options.A: Disease prevention and health promotion
options.B: Providing specialized hospital care
options.C: Advanced surgical interventions
options.D: Exclusively managing chronic illnesses

explanation: Spot on! Primary health care is all about stopping sickness before it starts and keeping people well, rather than waiting for them to need major hospital procedures. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why are shared medical tools and bedside tables such common culprits in hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Cleaning products actually feed microorganisms instead of killing them
options.B: Patients prefer sharing personal care items while admitted
options.C: Medical equipment naturally generates new bacteria over time
options.D: Pathogens can survive on dry surfaces and pass to patients via contact

explanation: Many tough germs love hanging out on dry hospital surfaces, waiting for the next touch to hop onto a patient.

question: How can rural communities creatively solve the problem of getting sick patients to a clinic?

options.A: Organizing local emergency transport systems like tricycles
options.B: Waiting for ambulances to be stationed in every street
options.C: Demanding that the government buy cars for every family
options.D: Building major federal highways to connect every village

explanation: Spot on! Communities often band together to arrange local transport like branded tricycles or bikes to bridge the gap during emergencies.

question: How do targeted therapy drugs differ from traditional chemotherapy?

options.A: They work exclusively by boosting the overall white blood cell count in the bloodstream
options.B: They can only be taken as topical creams applied directly to skin lesions
options.C: They completely rebuild the patient's bone marrow within forty-eight hours of administration
options.D: They focus on specific molecular targets involved in tumor growth rather than attacking all dividing cells

explanation: You're doing great! Targeted therapies act like smart missiles, zeroing in on specific cancer proteins instead of harming all fast-growing cells.

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

options.A: A formal diagnosis of depression given by a psychiatrist
options.B: The financial bankruptcy caused by buying medical equipment
options.C: Physical and emotional exhaustion from continuous caregiving duties
options.D: The intentional neglect of an older adult by family

explanation: Looking after someone day in and day out without enough rest can drain a person completely. That heavy fatigue is what we call burnout.

question: Which tummy trouble is most commonly caused by slow digestion and pressure from the uterus?

options.A: Bowel perforation
options.B: Intestinal obstruction
options.C: Peptic ulcers
options.D: Constipation

explanation: You got it! Slower movement means the bowel absorbs extra water, leaving stools hard to pass—plus, the heavy uterus adds extra pressure.

question: Why is waiting for low blood pressure a risky way to spot early internal bleeding in a young adult?

options.A: Strong compensatory mechanisms keep blood pressure normal until shock is severe
options.B: Internal bleeding actually makes blood pressure rise first
options.C: Young adults never get low blood pressure
options.D: Cuffs cannot measure pressure accurately during shock

explanation: Young bodies work overtime to hide blood loss by tightening blood vessels and racing the heart, so blood pressure can stay normal even when they're in trouble.

question: A patient develops a fever, cough, and shortness of breath five days after being admitted to the surgical ward for a knee replacement. How is this infection classified?

options.A: Hospital-acquired pneumonia
options.B: Aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Community-acquired pneumonia
options.D: Primary acute bronchitis

explanation: Any pneumonia symptoms appearing 48 hours or longer after a patient is admitted to a healthcare facility are classified as hospital-acquired or nosocomial pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why does the pancreas release bicarbonate into the small intestine?

options.A: To stimulate the liver to produce more cholesterol
options.B: To lubricate the intestinal walls for easier transit
options.C: To break down protein chains into individual amino acids
options.D: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming from the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Bicarbonate is alkaline, meaning it cools down and neutralizes the harsh acid coming from the stomach so it doesn't harm your gut lining.

question: What is a major advantage of using observation instead of questionnaires?

options.A: It guarantees that participants will never experience anxiety
options.B: It is completely immune to any form of human judgment error
options.C: It records actual behavior rather than self-reported claims
options.D: It requires zero preparation or specialized recording tools

explanation: Exactly! People might say one thing in a questionnaire, but observation lets you see what they actually do in practice.

question: What is a common non-infectious cause of cervical inflammation?

options.A: Increased dietary intake of refined sugars
options.B: Chemical spermicides and barrier devices
options.C: Normal fluctuations in monthly estrogen levels
options.D: Inadequate daily fluid consumption

explanation: Not all inflammation comes from germs! Things like chemical spermicides or barrier devices can irritate the delicate cervical tissue.

question: Why is active community surveillance just as important as checking hospital record books?

options.A: Community members are better at performing laboratory blood tests
options.B: Government funding requires village meetings every single month
options.C: Many sick people in rural areas never visit a formal health facility
options.D: Hospitals are not allowed to report infectious diseases directly

explanation: You're right on track! Many villagers stay home or go to local chemists when sick, so community-level reporting helps us catch hidden cases that hospitals might miss.
