question: Why is it so important to talk to a suspected abuse survivor alone in a private room, away from family?

options.A: To ensure the patient feels safe to speak freely without fear of the abuser
options.B: To reduce the amount of paperwork the nursing staff must complete
options.C: To prevent other patients from hearing about medical equipment
options.D: To comply with hospital billing regulations for outpatient visits

explanation: You nailed it! Abusers often watch what their victims say, so private time is key to helping the patient open up safely.

question: What is cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Fluid or blood filling the sac around the heart and squeezing it
options.B: Widening of the lower belly aorta
options.C: Inflammation of the inner heart valves
options.D: A blood clot blocking a coronary artery

explanation: Imagine water balloon pressure around the heart. When fluid leaks into the pericardial sac, it builds up pressure so the heart chambers can't relax and fill properly.

question: Which of the following is NOT a blockage-related (post-testicular) cause of male infertility?

options.A: Blocked vas deferens
options.B: Congenital absence of the sperm ducts
options.C: Epididymal scarring from infection
options.D: Klinefelter syndrome

explanation: Klinefelter syndrome is a chromosomal condition affecting the testes, whereas the other options are physical blockages in the tubes that carry sperm.

question: Besides checking physical lab results, what else should a nurse assess during routine consultations?

options.A: The patient's emotional readiness and coping style
options.B: The exact brand of clothing the patient prefers
options.C: The patient's long-term career and retirement plans
options.D: The architectural layout of the patient's house

explanation: Comprehensive nursing assessment evaluates mental health and emotional coping alongside physical health parameters. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h5)

question: A pregnant patient with gestational diabetes maintains a fasting blood glucose of 6.1 mmol/L despite following her diet and exercise plan for two weeks. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Advise the patient to eliminate all carbohydrates
options.B: Continue diet and exercise for another trimester
options.C: Stop all monitoring to reduce patient anxiety
options.D: Initiate pharmacotherapy such as insulin

explanation: When lifestyle changes fail to reach target blood glucose levels within a short timeframe, medication must be started to protect the baby from high sugar. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a primary and a secondary skin lesion?

options.A: Secondary lesions are always malignant, whereas primary ones are benign
options.B: Primary lesions contain fluid, while secondary lesions are strictly solid
options.C: Primary lesions only appear on the face, while secondary ones appear on limbs
options.D: Secondary lesions evolve from primary lesions due to scratching or healing

explanation: Primary lesions show up first on healthy skin. Secondary ones form later because of things like scratching, picking, or the natural healing process.

question: What is the purpose of the safety limits (guardrails) on smart infusion pumps?

options.A: To automatically calculate patient drug dosages without nurse input
options.B: To track how many supplies are used during each shift
options.C: To lock the pump door so patients cannot change settings
options.D: To warn nurses if a programmed dose is outside safe limits

explanation: Exactly! Guardrails act like a helpful safety net, popping up a warning if a number looks too high or too low.

question: Which behavior is typical in a patient with Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Confabulation, where they make up stories to fill memory gaps
options.B: Uncontrollable shaking of both hands while eating
options.C: Throwing angry tantrums at family members
options.D: Being completely mute and refusing to talk to anyone

explanation: Spot on! Patients with Korsakoff often unconsciously invent details (confabulate) to cover up the blank spots in their memory.

question: Why do we make time for psychological support and talking after a traumatic, high-risk birth?

options.A: To guarantee the mother never experiences physical fatigue
options.B: To ensure the infant learns to walk at an earlier age
options.C: To help prevent long-term anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: To replace the need for any physical postpartum examinations

explanation: Birth can sometimes be frightening. Helping mums talk through their experience is a wonderful way to heal emotional scars and prevent long-term anxiety.

question: Under current Nigerian laws, when is a pregnancy termination generally allowed?

options.A: If the pregnancy results from consensual teenage dating
options.B: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases during the first trimester
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it in writing

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian laws are quite strict and typically permit abortion only when carrying the pregnancy to term puts the mother's life in danger.

question: What happens inside your chest when your diaphragm contracts to take in a normal breath?

options.A: Surface tension increases to make the lung tissue stiffer
options.B: Intrapleural pressure decreases to draw air into the lungs
options.C: Intrapleural pressure increases to force air out of the lungs
options.D: The chest wall pushes inward to compress the lung tissue

explanation: Great thinking! When your diaphragm moves down and your chest expands, the pressure inside drops below the outside air pressure, naturally sucking air in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h1)

question: A community health nurse sets up a blood pressure screening booth at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Great thinking! Screening catches health problems early before they cause severe damage, which is the core of secondary prevention.

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in eclampsia?

options.A: Oxytocin infusion
options.B: Diazepam injection
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Sodium bicarbonate

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is our absolute best friend in emergency obstetrics for keeping eclamptic seizures at bay and protecting the mother.

question: What is the most common long-term result for patients who receive radioactive iodine treatment?

options.A: The need for lifelong maintenance doses of propylthiouracil
options.B: Spontaneous recovery of normal thyroid function within five years
options.C: Complete physical removal of the thyroid gland through scarring
options.D: Permanent hypothyroidism requiring lifelong hormone replacement

explanation: Because the radiation quiets down the gland so well, many patients end up with an underactive thyroid and take daily thyroxine tablets.

question: What event triggers the body to start making mature milk in large amounts (Lactogenesis II)?

options.A: The first infant suckling session
options.B: Delivery of the placenta
options.C: A sudden surge in maternal progesterone
options.D: Closure of the lactiferous ducts

explanation: When the placenta comes out, progesterone levels crash. That sudden drop removes the brake on prolactin, and boom—mature milk comes in!

question: What is the best eating strategy for a patient dealing with severe nausea and poor appetite?

options.A: Encouraging three large, heavy meals to catch up on lost calories
options.B: Forcing the patient to finish everything on a large dinner plate
options.C: Withholding all food until appetite returns spontaneously
options.D: Serving small, frequent nutrient-dense meals throughout the day

explanation: Huge meals can make a nauseous patient feel worse. Small, tasty bites spaced through the day are much easier to manage!

question: Which type of ultrasound is best when you need to check how fast and in what direction blood is flowing?

options.A: Doppler ultrasound
options.B: Static X-ray mode
options.C: M-Mode ultrasound
options.D: B-Mode ultrasound

explanation: Doppler is your go-to scan for blood vessels because it specifically tracks moving red blood cells to measure flow.

question: What is the main purpose of documentation in palliative care?

options.A: To ensure clear communication of care goals across different disciplines
options.B: To prove to insurance companies that treatments are expensive
options.C: To replace verbal communication between nursing shifts completely
options.D: To protect the hospital legally from patient lawsuits

explanation: Good records ensure that every doctor, nurse, and therapist on the team knows the current plan and the patient's wishes.

question: A patient with severe tummy pain walks into the clinic bent forward. What is causing this posture?

options.A: Normal aging changes
options.B: A neurological stroke
options.C: Extreme psychological joy
options.D: Pain and guarding

explanation: This is called 'guarding.' It's a natural, protective reflex where the body curls inward to shield a painful spot from touch or stretch.

question: Why does the brain cut back on its own chemical receptors after repeated drug use?

options.A: To increase the speed of normal digestion
options.B: To store extra energy for physical exercise
options.C: To improve overall visual acuity at night
options.D: To protect itself from chemical overload

explanation: Well thought out! When a drug floods the brain, it tries to protect itself by reducing receptors (down-regulation) to restore some balance. The body is always trying to keep things stable!

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to preserve food at home?

options.A: Exposing raw meat to open air at room temperature for several days.
options.B: Drying fruits and vegetables under the sun.
options.C: Smoking or salting fish to prevent bacterial growth.
options.D: Storing perishable items in a working refrigerator.

explanation: Correct! Leaving raw meat out in the open air lets bacteria multiply fast and ruins the food instead of saving it.

question: Why is a luminal amebicide often given after a tissue amebicide like metronidazole?

options.A: To accelerate the renal excretion of the first drug
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach
options.C: To destroy cysts remaining in the gut lumen and prevent relapse
options.D: To quickly replenish lost electrolytes in the bloodstream

explanation: You're doing great! While metronidazole clears the tissue, luminal agents are needed to wipe out any sneaky cysts hiding in the gut so the infection doesn't return.

question: Why is trapping blood inside the penis (veno-occlusive mechanism) so important?

options.A: It closes off the urethral opening to prevent fluid loss during arousal
options.B: It pumps extra blood directly from the deep dorsal vein into the glans
options.C: It traps blood inside the corpora cavernosa to build high internal pressure
options.D: It releases large amounts of nitric oxide to keep the smooth muscle relaxed

explanation: Wonderful! By stopping blood from draining out while more keeps flowing in, pressure builds up to create a firm erection.

question: Why must a nurse be careful not to confuse statistical significance with real clinical usefulness?

options.A: Clinical importance only matters if the p-value is exactly equal to zero
options.B: A tiny change in numbers can reach statistical significance in a huge study without helping patients much
options.C: Statistical programs always hide the real health outcomes from the nursing staff
options.D: Statistical significance is completely made up and has no place in modern hospital wards

explanation: If a study is massive, even a tiny, unimportant number change can look 'statistically significant' even if patients don't feel any real health benefit.

question: Which brain chemical is most closely linked to psychotic symptoms?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: You nailed it! Too much activity in the brain's dopamine pathways is a major factor in psychosis.

question: When is it legally and ethically necessary for a nurse to break adolescent confidentiality?

options.A: Whenever the clinic manager requests a routine attendance report
options.B: When the adolescent refuses to take prescribed multivitamin tablets
options.C: When the teenager is at risk of suicide or severe harm
options.D: Whenever a parent asks about the teen's school grades

explanation: Safety comes first; if a young person is suicidal or facing severe danger, confidentiality must be broken to protect them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is the difference between data fabrication and data falsification?

options.A: Fabrication applies to nursing, falsification applies to physics
options.B: Fabrication is inventing fake data, while falsification is altering real data
options.C: Fabrication is legal with IRB approval, falsification is never allowed
options.D: Fabrication is stealing text, falsification is stealing money

explanation: You got it! Fabrication means making numbers up from thin air, while falsification means tampering with real results.

question: A nurse is teaching a client with chronic venous insufficiency how to care for themselves daily. What advice fits best?

options.A: Elevate your legs above the level of your heart several times a day.
options.B: Avoid wearing compression stockings during your normal daytime hours.
options.C: Stand in place for long periods to keep your leg muscles active.
options.D: Cross your legs at the knees whenever sitting down in a chair.

explanation: Gravity is your friend here! Propping those legs up high helps fluid drain back toward the heart instead of pooling at the ankles.

question: A patient arrives with burnt nose hairs, blackish sputum, and a very hoarse voice. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Apply silver sulfadiazine cream to the face
options.B: Calculate the exact total body surface area percentage
options.C: Administer oral analgesics for pain control
options.D: Prepare for emergency endotracheal intubation

explanation: Those are classic signs of smoke inhalation! The airway can swell shut very quickly, so getting ready to tube the patient is a true lifesaver.

question: A pregnant teenager at her antenatal visit says her family expects a local nurse to circumcise her newborn daughter. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Send the family to a traditional cutter who uses sterile tools
options.B: Offer to do it quietly at the clinic to avoid infections
options.C: Ignore it since cultural practices are none of a nurse's business
options.D: Educate the mother firmly on the severe health risks and legal penalties of FGM

explanation: Spot on! Nurses must actively educate patients against FGM, uphold professional ethics, and make it clear that medicalized cutting is both illegal and unethical.

question: Which hygiene habit should nurses advise patients to ditch because it washes away protective vaginal flora?

options.A: Wiping front to back
options.B: Douching
options.C: Wearing cotton underwear
options.D: Washing with plain water

explanation: Douching disrupts that natural acidic balance and flushes out our helpful lactobacilli friends, opening the door wide for infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h7)

question: How does the constant push for a male child indirectly cause higher rates of dangerous bleeding after birth?

options.A: It forces pregnant women to avoid attending antenatal care clinics entirely
options.B: It causes surgical instruments used during delivery to become contaminated
options.C: It restricts mothers from eating iron-rich foods after giving birth
options.D: It drives women to achieve grand multiparity, increasing uterine fatigue and bleeding risks

explanation: Trying over and over for a boy leads to many pregnancies, which wears out the womb muscles and raises the risk of severe bleeding after delivery.

question: What is the correct way to handle a newly applied plaster cast while it is still drying?

options.A: Lift the cast using only the fingertips
options.B: Support the cast using the palms of the hands
options.C: Rest the damp cast on a narrow, hard metal bar
options.D: Wrap the cast tightly in thick plastic sheeting

explanation: Fingertips create flat pressure spots on a drying plaster cast, which can indent the plaster and cause skin breakdown underneath. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h7)

question: What should you do right away if you evaluate your patient and see they haven't met their care goal?

options.A: Wait until the next morning doctor's rounds to report it
options.B: Discontinue all monitoring devices to reduce patient stress
options.C: Reassess the patient and modify the plan of care
options.D: Document that the patient is impossible to treat

explanation: Don't panic if a goal isn't met—that's totally normal nursing! It just means it's time to cycle back, figure out what's going on, and tweak your game plan.

question: Which of these statements about drug transfer across the placenta is FALSE?

options.A: Most fat-soluble drugs cross easily from mother to fetus
options.B: Medications taken during pregnancy can affect the unborn baby
options.C: The placenta serves as an impenetrable shield blocking all maternal drugs
options.D: Simple diffusion is a common way drugs cross the placenta

explanation: Never assume the placenta blocks everything! It's actually a pretty poor barrier, and most drugs in a mother's blood can pass through to the fetus.

question: A GPI patient gets their first penicillin dose and suddenly develops a fever, chills, and worse symptoms. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Their brain shrinkage is suddenly getting worse forever.
options.B: They are having a bad allergic reaction to the penicillin.
options.C: They caught a brand-new pneumonia infection in the ward.
options.D: A normal Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction as the bacteria die off.

explanation: Spot on! When masses of bacteria die off all at once from the antibiotic, they release toxins that cause a temporary fever flare-up. It's tough, but it means the drug is working!

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) so helpful in primary healthcare clinics across Nigeria?

options.A: It completely cures any existing viral infection within a few minutes
options.B: It is inexpensive, fast, and does not require a complex laboratory setup
options.C: It replaces the need for any healthcare personnel during the procedure
options.D: It provides a permanent digital image stored in a computer database

explanation: Brilliant! VIA is cheap, quick, and gives instant results right there in the community clinic without needing a fancy lab. Perfect for low-resource settings!

question: A patient reports severe burning and pain immediately after receiving ear drops. What is the nurse's first action?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the pain goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the procedure and report the reaction to the doctor
options.C: Pack the ear canal tightly with sterile gauze
options.D: Reassure the patient and give a second dose right away

explanation: Severe pain means something is wrong, so the nurse must stop immediately and seek medical guidance. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: Which body system does your skin belong to?

options.A: The integumentary system
options.B: The respiratory system
options.C: The circulatory system
options.D: The endocrine system

explanation: You got it! The skin is part of the integumentary system, which also includes your hair, nails, and glands that keep your body safe. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which life stage is especially known for triggering or worsening domestic violence?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Pregnancy
options.C: Retirement
options.D: Toddlerhood

explanation: Well done! Studies show pregnancy is a high-risk period where domestic violence often starts or suddenly gets worse.

question: What is a major physical benefit of early ambulation on the respiratory system?

options.A: It prevents chronic asthma attacks from developing in adults
options.B: It completely stops the production of mucus in the airways
options.C: It allows the lungs to expand fully to prevent pneumonia
options.D: It lowers the total volume of oxygen required by the body

explanation: Being upright helps the lungs open up completely, which stops fluid and secretions from pooling and causing infections like pneumonia. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why are iron supplements routinely given during antenatal care?

options.A: To increase the speed of fetal bone mineralization
options.B: To prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To reduce the frequency of Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: To support the massive expansion of maternal blood volume

explanation: Because a pregnant woman's blood volume increases so much, she needs extra iron to make enough hemoglobin and prevent anemia.

question: A patient has a total fluid intake of 2,200 milliliters and a total output of 1,500 milliliters. What is their net balance?

options.A: Negative 700 milliliters
options.B: Positive 3,700 milliliters
options.C: Negative 3,700 milliliters
options.D: Positive 700 milliliters

explanation: Subtracting 1,500 output from 2,200 intake leaves a remaining surplus of 700 milliliters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h7)

question: Which type of ovarian cancer is the most common, making up about 90% of all cases?

options.A: Germ cell tumors
options.B: Stromal cell tumors
options.C: Endodermal sinus tumors
options.D: Epithelial ovarian cancer

explanation: Spot on! Epithelial tumors start from the outer surface lining of the ovary and make up the vast majority of cases we see in practice.

question: Why is the issue of consent particularly critical when discussing forced marriage?

options.A: Consent is only relevant in urban healthcare settings
options.B: Minors and coerced individuals cannot give free and informed agreement
options.C: Adults over 18 never experience forced marriage situations
options.D: Legal documents require parental signatures for all marriages

explanation: True consent requires maturity, capacity, and freedom from pressure, elements that are absent when external forces dictate a union. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: What does setting a baseline mean in the context of community health planning?

options.A: Calculating the exact cost of building a fence around the clinic
options.B: Establishing the starting measurements to evaluate future progress
options.C: Writing down the names of all nurses working in the primary health center
options.D: Listing the minimum amount of salary a community health worker accepts

explanation: A baseline gives you initial numbers, like immunization coverage rates, so you can measure improvement after your program runs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the safety rules for giving medications?

options.A: Right patient identity
options.B: Right dosage amount
options.C: Right drug name
options.D: Right room decoration

explanation: Haha, room decor won't help your patient! We stick to the vital rights like right patient, drug, dose, route, and time.

question: How do residential care homes differ basically from nursing homes?

options.A: Nursing homes feature 24-hour medical staff for complex health needs, while residential care focuses on daily living assistance
options.B: Residential care homes are operated by the government, while nursing homes are private
options.C: Residential care homes are exclusively for children, whereas nursing homes are strictly for the elderly
options.D: Nursing homes do not provide meals, unlike standard residential care facilities

explanation: Spot on! The big difference is clinical staffing: nursing homes have 24-hour medical care for heavy health needs, while residential homes focus more on daily living support.

question: Which syndrome is famously linked with missing female reproductive structures like the uterus or tubes?

options.A: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome
options.B: Endometriosis stage IV
options.C: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Don't let the long name scare you! MRKH syndrome involves the congenital absence of the uterus and upper vagina. You're doing great.

question: A patient comes to the surgical ward with a suspected knee injury involving a torn ligament. Which diagnostic test is the nurse most likely to prepare the patient for?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Ligaments are soft tissues inside a joint, making MRI the ideal test to check for tears. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the main role of the pons in the brainstem?

options.A: Producing hormones to control the pituitary gland
options.B: Processing conscious thought and long-term memory
options.C: Relaying information between the cerebrum and cerebellum
options.D: Serving as the primary visual processing center

explanation: The pons acts as a bridge, passing messages smoothly between the upper brain and the cerebellum.

question: Which decontamination process is required to completely destroy bacterial spores?

options.A: Washing
options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Only sterilization is powerful enough to destroy all microbial life, including tough bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why should nurses take parents seriously when they worry about their toddler's social development?

options.A: Doctors require parental permission to perform physical exams
options.B: Family concerns are more accurate than formal medical tests
options.C: Parents usually exaggerate normal childhood naughtiness
options.D: Caregivers are often the first to notice early developmental differences

explanation: Parents spend the most time with their little ones and usually spot early warning signs before anyone else walks into the room. Trust their insights!

question: Which type of fracture happens when the broken bone pushes through the skin?

options.A: Comminuted fracture
options.B: Closed fracture
options.C: Open fracture
options.D: Greenstick fracture

explanation: When bone breaks through the skin, it's called an open (or compound) fracture. This requires extra care because of the high risk of infection!

question: As a nurse, what is a key action when helping a patient deal with the emotional side of sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Discouraging partner involvement in therapy
options.B: Prescribing anti-anxiety medications directly
options.C: Validating feelings and offering referrals
options.D: Diagnosing deep psychiatric disorders

explanation: Brilliant! Creating a safe, judgment-free space and connecting them with a trained counselor makes all the difference in their care.

question: A woman is pushing very fast with a large baby facing upward and backward. What is she most at risk for?

options.A: Premature rupture of membranes
options.B: Severe perineal laceration
options.C: Hypertensive crisis
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage from atony

explanation: Fast pushing combined with a larger baby and a tricky position puts extra stress on the tissues, greatly increasing the chance of a deep tear.

question: What makes an expected outcome (goal) well-written?

options.A: It must be measurable and time-bound
options.B: It should describe what the nurse will do
options.C: It should be as broad as possible
options.D: It must focus on hospital routines

explanation: Goals need clear targets and deadlines (like 'patient will walk to the door by tomorrow') so you can easily tell if they were actually reached.

question: A patient swallowed a small toy that got stuck in their throat. Why would a doctor perform a laryngoscopy?

options.A: To test the patient's swallowing reflex
options.B: To locate and safely remove the inhaled object
options.C: To measure the oxygen content in the lungs
options.D: To check for chronic bacterial throat infections

explanation: Spot on! When something gets stuck where it shouldn't be, this procedure lets the clinician spot the object and safely take it out.

question: What is the main benefit of building a coalition for a health campaign?

options.A: It eliminates all financial costs of the project
options.B: It multiplies power by bringing together diverse voices
options.C: It gives nurses absolute authority over local government
options.D: It removes the need for community meetings

explanation: You got it! Teamwork makes the dream work. Combining different groups and voices makes your campaign much harder to ignore.

question: How do mast cell stabilizers stop allergic symptoms from starting?

options.A: By directly destroying free-floating allergen particles
options.B: By permanently shrinking the size of mucous glands
options.C: By replacing natural antibodies in the bloodstream
options.D: By stopping mast cells from bursting and releasing histamine

explanation: You nailed it! They act like strong shields, keeping mast cell walls intact so the histamine inside cannot escape to cause trouble.

question: Where do the coronary arteries, which feed the heart muscle itself, take their origin?

options.A: The pulmonary veins
options.B: The base of the aorta
options.C: The right atrium
options.D: The superior vena cava

explanation: The heart works non-stop, so it needs its own private blood supply! The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to get the very first taste of fresh oxygen.

question: What is the standard test used to check for a strep throat infection?

options.A: Sputum Gram stain
options.B: Throat swab culture
options.C: Peak flow measurement
options.D: Chest radiography

explanation: Correct! A quick swab of the back of the throat helps us check if streptococcus bacteria are causing the trouble.

question: Why is active listening an important skill in health promotion?

options.A: It helps the nurse uncover barriers stopping the patient from being healthy
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical health
options.C: It shortens the time required for documentation paperwork
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never develop a chronic illness

explanation: Listening carefully lets nurses find out if fear, cost, or confusion is getting in the way of a patient's care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is a major practical advantage of a mechanical beam balance scale over a digital scale?

options.A: It does not require electrical power or batteries
options.B: It is much smaller and easier to carry to field postings
options.C: It automatically calculates the body mass index
options.D: It measures the patient's height at the same time

explanation: Beam balance scales rely purely on mechanical counterweights, making them very reliable in remote clinics where electricity is unreliable. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is often the earliest warning sign of endometrial cancer in women who have gone through menopause?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Severe lower back pain
options.C: Rapid weight gain
options.D: Swollen lower extremities

explanation: Any spotting or bleeding after menopause is never normal and is usually the very first clue that prompts doctors to check the uterine lining.

question: A clinic nurse wants to increase teenage visits to the reproductive health unit. What is the best step to take first?

options.A: Punish students who refuse to attend the hospital during school hours
options.B: Involve local youth leaders and teenagers in planning the clinic's hours and layout
options.C: Lock the adult waiting room so teenagers have no choice of seats
options.D: Remove all chairs from the clinic to make visits very quick

explanation: Involving the target audience directly ensures the services match their preferences and removes barriers to attendance. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why should a nurse avoid poking around blindly if a small object is stuck in a patient's ear or nose?

options.A: It always causes permanent sensorineural hearing loss
options.B: It introduces bacteria that cause chronic sinusitis
options.C: It immediately triggers severe systemic hypertension
options.D: It can push the object deeper and cause tissue damage

explanation: Spot on! Without a clear view, poking instruments inside can easily push the object further down into delicate tissues or cause injuries. Always use proper visualization!

question: Which breathing sound tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway obstruction?

options.A: Crackles
options.B: Wheezing
options.C: Friction rub
options.D: Stridor

explanation: Stridor is that high-pitched, strained sound you hear when air is struggling to push past a blockage in the upper airway. You can often hear it without a stethoscope!

question: How is endocrine signaling different from nervous system signaling?

options.A: Nervous signaling produces much slower, permanent bodily changes
options.B: Nervous signaling relies entirely on circulating blood vessels
options.C: Endocrine signaling uses direct physical contact with cells
options.D: Endocrine signaling is slower and has longer-lasting effects

explanation: Nerve impulses are like a quick flash of lightning, while hormones are like a slow, steady wave whose effects linger much longer.

question: In waste management, what does the term 'leachate' mean?

options.A: The gas that builds up inside sealed biological waste autoclaves
options.B: Contaminated liquid that drains from waste dumps into soil and water sources
options.C: Protective fluid applied to gloves before handling sharp objects
options.D: A special chemical spray used to clean medical instrument trays

explanation: You got it! When rainwater trickles through poorly stored waste, it picks up nasty chemicals and germs, forming 'leachate' that can pollute underground water.

question: What role do prostaglandins play when someone develops a fever?

options.A: They attack and destroy bacteria in the blood
options.B: They relax muscles to stop shivering
options.C: They turn on sweat glands to cool the skin
options.D: They tell the hypothalamus to raise the body's temperature setting

explanation: You're doing great! Prostaglandins act like messengers telling your brain's thermostat to crank up the heat.

question: Which of the following is considered a direct source of data for maternal mortality?

options.A: General household census questionnaires
options.B: Retrospective community interviews about sisters
options.C: Hospital admission and delivery registers
options.D: Mathematical models based on neighboring countries

explanation: Hospital registers and civil registration records capture actual events directly as they are documented in health facilities or official registries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the huff coughing technique?

options.A: To measure the total lung capacity of the patient
options.B: To force air deeply into closed alveoli sacs
options.C: To prevent the tongue from blocking the throat
options.D: To move mucus upward without collapsing the airways

explanation: Huff coughing keeps the vocal cords open while the patient exhales sharply, helping push mucus up from the lower airways safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT an accessory organ of digestion?

options.A: The gallbladder
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The liver

explanation: Food actually passes right through the stomach as part of the main tube (alimentary canal). The liver, pancreas, and gallbladder sit off to the side as trusty helpers, making them accessory organs!

question: Why is fluoroscopy a key component of a barium swallow test?

options.A: It provides real-time moving images of swallowing and peristalsis
options.B: It permanently removes small blockages in the throat
options.C: It measures the exact pH levels inside the stomach
options.D: It checks the patient's blood pressure throughout the scan

explanation: Unlike standard still X-rays, fluoroscopy acts like an X-ray movie, letting the radiologist watch how food and liquid move down the throat in real time. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: Poor environmental sanitation in a community is most directly linked to outbreaks of which disease?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Hypertension

explanation: Cholera is a waterborne disease spread easily when sanitation and safe drinking water systems fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the single best way to stop infectious diarrhoea from spreading in a community?

options.A: Avoiding all physical exercise during warm weather
options.B: Drinking carbonated beverages instead of water
options.C: Proper handwashing with soap and water
options.D: Taking daily doses of over-the-counter loperamide

explanation: Simple soap and water break the cycle of germ transmission! Good hand hygiene is still your number one shield against stomach bugs.

question: How long does the postpartum (puerperium) period typically last for a new mother?

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: You've got this! The puerperium lasts for about six weeks—this is the special window of time needed for the mother's body and organs to gently return to their pre-pregnancy state.

question: When checking over a recently bereaved female patient, what sign might make you suspect she went through harmful widowhood rites?

options.A: Unexplained scalp injuries and severe sudden weight loss
options.B: Expressed desire to join a local grief support counseling group
options.C: Requests for routine immunizations against common infections
options.D: A sudden increase in blood pressure readings during the visit

explanation: Rough hair shaving can hurt the scalp, and forced fasting often leads to quick, unhealthy weight loss. Good assessment skills catch these clues!

question: Why do the cells on the very outer layer of your skin not have nuclei?

options.A: They have been damaged by direct exposure to ultraviolet radiation
options.B: They are specialized immune cells that do not require genetic material
options.C: They are actively dividing stem cells that have temporarily discarded their DNA
options.D: They are dead, keratin-filled cells that have been pushed upward from deeper layers

explanation: Exactly right! As skin cells travel up from the bottom, they flatten, fill with tough keratin, lose their nuclei, and form a protective dead layer.

question: What is the main job of mineralocorticoids in the human body?

options.A: Regulating sodium and fluid balance
options.B: Suppressing white blood cell activity
options.C: Increasing protein synthesis in muscles
options.D: Lowering high blood sugar levels

explanation: Mineralocorticoids (like aldosterone) work on the kidneys to manage salt (sodium) and water in your body. It's all about keeping your fluid balance steady!

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to spot abnormal labour early?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any surgical intervention.
options.B: It allows the nurse to administer pain relief without a doctor's order.
options.C: It prevents prolonged obstructed labour and severe maternal complications.
options.D: It guarantees that the baby will be born within the next ten minutes.

explanation: Spotting delays early helps you protect the mother from exhaustion, severe infection, and long-term birth injuries. You've got this!

question: Why is it harmful when hospital departments operate in separate 'silos' without talking to each other?

options.A: It causes the hospital to run out of physical building space
options.B: It automatically increases the cost of medical equipment
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients admitted daily
options.D: It leads to severe delays and fragmented patient care

explanation: Great thinking! When units don't share info, patient care becomes scattered and delayed. Keeping the lines of communication open keeps our patients safe.

question: What is a key safety step a home health nurse should take with a pregnant patient in case of an emergency?

options.A: Instruct the family to never call emergency services under any condition.
options.B: Encourage the patient to drive herself to the hospital if pain starts.
options.C: Establish a clear emergency plan and post local hospital numbers visibly.
options.D: Leave complex medical equipment in the home without instructions.

explanation: Having a clear, visible emergency plan ensures that family members can act quickly and correctly when urgent signs appear. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: Why is it smart to involve bedside nurses when drafting new unit objectives?

options.A: They understand the practical realities of daily clinical workflow.
options.B: They are the only ones allowed to sign administrative documents.
options.C: Hospital regulations legally forbid managers from planning alone.
options.D: It prevents managers from having to do any actual work.

explanation: Bedside nurses know what's really happening on the floor. Involving them ensures our goals are practical and actually work in real life!

question: Which hormone tells the gallbladder to release stored bile?

options.A: Secretin
options.B: Gastrin
options.C: Cholecystokinin (CCK)
options.D: Insulin

explanation: When fats and proteins hit your small intestine, it releases CCK, which signals the gallbladder to squeeze and release bile.
